note: No AI model weights are downloaded, embedded, or referenced by pinned URL anywhere in this repository as of this session -- this manifest documents the INTENDED model choices and why, not files that exist. Section 17 of the build spec requires at least one Serbian-capable transcription model and one tested stem-separation model physically bundled in the offline Windows package; that bundling has NOT happened yet (blocked by this sandbox's network policy, same reason python.org/gyan.dev are unreachable here -- confirmed directly in this session).

transcription.candidate_model: Systran/faster-whisper-large-v3 or a smaller distilled variant (e.g. large-v3-turbo) from the faster-whisper-compatible CTranslate2 model set on Hugging Face
transcription.serbian_support: Whisper large-v3/v3-turbo support Serbian as one of its ~99 training languages; this has not been independently benchmarked against Serbian song lyrics in this session -- needs real evaluation before shipping, not just a language-list check
transcription.cpu_fallback: faster-whisper runs pure CPU by default when no CUDA device is available; already the default code path since the app has no CUDA dependency

stem_separation.candidate_model: UVR-MDX-NET or Demucs v4 htdemucs, both supported by audio-separator's model registry
stem_separation.cpu_fallback: the [cpu] extra is exactly this -- ONNX Runtime CPU execution provider, no CUDA required

next_steps_for_real_implementation: Extend windows_build/setup's --stage-components (or a sibling --stage-ai-models mode) to download a specific pinned model file with a real SHA-256, the same pattern already used for Python/FFmpeg/yt-dlp/Deno
Add the model manifest with real per-model SHA-256, license, and size once a specific model file is chosen and downloaded for real on a network-unrestricted runner (Windows CI)

Run a real transcription against a Serbian test clip and a real stem-separation pass against a test song before claiming this section done -- do not mark this complete on the strength of 'the package imports cleanly', which is all that has been verified so far (see docs/PYTHON_IMPORT_REPORT.json)
